<span id="clean-room-rules"></span>
== Clean-room rules ==

These come from the method described on occupysaas.com and from each project’s <code>CLEAN_ROOM.md</code>. The project policy always wins if the two differ.

'''Allowed in'''

* Public API documentation
* Open standards and RFCs
* Public SDK behaviour
* Black-box test results

'''Never allowed'''

* Leaked or proprietary source
* Decompiled binaries
* Former-employer confidential information
* Copied UI assets or trademarks

<span id="former-employees-of-the-vendors"></span>
== Former employees of the vendors ==

You are welcome, but never with confidential knowledge from a former employer. Anyone with relevant inside knowledge should stay on the public-spec side of the firewall or sit that project out. When in doubt, read the project’s <code>CLEAN_ROOM.md</code> and ask before contributing.

<span id="working-rules"></span>
== Working rules ==

* Specs and contracts come first (for example <code>openapi.yaml</code>), then code, then tests.
* A human reviews every change before merge, even when AI wrote it.
* Compatibility tests against real vendor SDKs decide what counts as done.
* Say what is planned and what is shipped. Do not describe unbuilt features as working.
* Use vendor names only to describe compatibility.
